prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1423; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a collision at an intersection while turning left, with the claimant's vehicle struck on the driver side. The claimant reports a knee injury and has no legal representation at this stage.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene confirm the damage pattern and show the vehicle's front end and side panels consistent with the reported impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, so the photos are the main visual record at this point.

Entry 3: Police report lists the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle, and the statements of the other parties agree on that point. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing so far suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 4: Claimant gave the same account of the collision in each contact so far, describing the left turn and the moment of impact in matching detail. Vehicle inspection found no earlier damage on record, and the repair estimate lines up with the impact described.

Entry 5: Medical records show a knee injury that fits the kind and force of the crash. No prior injury to the same body area is on file. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Based on the photos, police report, medical records, and consistent statements, the claim appears to be supported by the available evidence. File remains open for final review of the treatment billing and the repair invoice.
